content.section: 10.4 Recommendations for follow-up after acute pulmonary embolism
content.intro: Nurses work collaboratively with patients using behavioural frameworks and motivational interviewing to identify and modify associated risk factors (smoking cessation, diet, physical activity, and exercise). They promote self-management skills such as use of compression stockings, safe increase in mobility, increased awareness of signs of recurrence or complications.

recommendations.recommendation: Routine clinical evaluation of patients 3–6 months after the acute PE episode is recommended.

An integrated model of patient care after PE (involving hospital specialists, appropriately qualified nurses, and primary care physicians) is recommended to ensure optimal transition from hospital to community care.

In symptomatic patients with mismatched perfusion defects persisting on V/Q scan beyond 3 months after acute PE, referral to a PH/CTEPH expert centre is recommended after taking into account results of echocardiography, natriuretic peptide levels, and/or CPET.
recommendations.notes: Targets evaluation for chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH).

recommendations.recommendation: Further diagnostic evaluation should be considered in patients with persistent or new-onset dyspnoea/exercise limitation after PE.
Further diagnostic evaluation may be considered in asymptomatic patients with risk factors for CTEPH.
